CVE-2019-9923.title: tar: null-pointer dereference in pax_decode_header in sparse.c
CVE-2019-9923.description: pax_decode_header in sparse.c in GNU Tar before 1.32 had a NULL pointer dereference when parsing certain archives that have malformed extended headers.

CVE-2021-20193.title: tar: Memory leak in read_header() in list.c
CVE-2021-20193.description: A flaw was found in the src/list.c of tar. This flaw allows an attacker who can submit a crafted input file to tar to cause uncontrolled consumption of memory. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to system availability.

CVE-2023-39804.title: tar: Incorrectly handled extension attributes in PAX archives can lead to a crash
CVE-2023-39804.description: A flaw was found in tar. This issue occurs when extended attributes are processed in PAX archives, and could allow an attacker to cause an application crash, resulting in a denial of service.

CVE-2026-5704.title: tar: tar: Hidden file injection via crafted archives
CVE-2026-5704.description: A flaw was found in tar. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by crafting a malicious archive, leading to hidden file injection with fully attacker-controlled content. This bypasses pre-extraction inspection mechanisms, potentially allowing an attacker to introduce malicious files onto a system without detection.

CVE-2026-18477.title: tar: tar: TOCTOU in incremental dumpdir 'X' rename handling allows restore path escape
CVE-2026-18477.description: A TOCTOU (Time-of-Check Time-of-Use) vulnerability in GNU tar's incremental dumpdir 'X' rename handling allows a local attacker with write access to a directory being backed up to influence the restore process if the attacker has access to the system where the restore is being performed. During restoration, files or directories may be created, renamed or overwritten outside the intended extraction directory. This could lead to unauthorized file modification or, in some cases, privilege escalation. Exploitation does not require the attacker to modify or craft the archive, and standard backup and restore workflows—including extracting into a newly created directory without using the -P option do not mitigate the issue.

CVE-2026-18508.title: tar: tar: --one-top-level hardlink targets not confined to top-level directory enabling arbitrary file overwrite
CVE-2026-18508.description: A flaw was found in GNU tar. When extracting an archive with the --one-top-level option, hardlink targets are not confined to the designated top-level directory and may resolve relative to the extraction working directory. A crafted archive can create hardlinks that escape the intended boundary and, when combined with a preexisting symbolic link under the working directory, may allow writing outside that boundary during a single extraction.
